1. (Currently Amended) An assembly comprising a test tube with a light-activated microtransponder (MTP) affixed thereto, wherein the MTP is responsive to light activation for identification and tracking purposes.

2. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in the test tube and is light-activated.

3. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom surface of the test tube, oriented for reading downwards, and wherein the MTP is light-activated.

4. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the test tube is a biorepository test tube designed for long-term storage of biological samples.

5. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer and is light-activated for sample identification.

6. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the container and is light-activated for optical reading.

(Currently Amended) A system for storing samples comprising the assembly of claim 1, and one or more of the following: a rack for biorepository test tubes with light-activated MTP reading capability; an automated robot for moving racks or biorepository test tubes equipped to read light-activated MTPs; and an automated sampling device adapted to sample said racks or biorepository test tubes and read light-activated MTPs.

14. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 13 adapted for low temperature operation, wherein the racks/test tubes are handled at -20°C or less and the light-activated MTPs remain readable at such temperatures.

15. (Currently Amended) A method of forming a test tube assembly of claim 1, comprising embedding a light-activated MTP in plastic by heating the MTP to above the melting point of the plastic and melting a portion of the plastic with the heated MTP.

16. (Currently Amended) A method of reading an embedded light-activated MTP in a test tube assembly of claim 1, comprising: providing an embedded light-activated MTP; and reading the MTP using light activation.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of reading of claim 16, wherein the embedding material is frost coated and the light-activated MTP is readable through the frost coating.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 16, wherein the reader comprises a vial receptacle and wherein the vial receptacle and the embedded light-activated MTP are maintained at a temperature of -20°C or less.

19. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer and is light-activated.

20. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 19, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the container and is light-activated.

21. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 19, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom surface of the container, oriented for reading downwards, and is light-activated.

22. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the container and is light-activated for optical identification.

23. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom surface of the container, oriented for reading downwards, and is light-activated.
